questions.question: 为什么有KV页仍可能无法复用整段混合模型前缀？
questions.answer: 递归状态是覆盖更新的。即使KV页还在，恢复位置也必须有完全对应的递归检查点；不能把较晚状态截短成较早状态。
questions.example: 教学例：KV覆盖到640token，但最近状态只在528；原生服务仍需从528重算到640。

questions.question: 一个request恢复同一检查点两次，就算proven了吗？
questions.answer: 不算。需要至少两个不同恢复request，或者它本来就是已知分叉；否则每条会话的祖先都会被单次后继访问永久保护。
questions.example: 教学例：request b重复restore只留tier2；b和c都restore后才进入tier3。

questions.question: FrontierReplay和ReplaySSM都记录输入，解决的是同一个问题吗？
questions.answer: 不是。ReplaySSM围绕decode状态写回、output-only和投机回滚；FrontierReplay围绕prefill结构边界的检查点产生与保留。相似代数不代表服务策略、精度或证据可直接共用。
questions.example: 教学例：16步decode刷新正确，不能证明下一会话的模板边界已保存、仍驻留且可命中。

questions.question: 为什么不能在prepare后立即把检查点放进lookup？
questions.answer: prepare只预留位置，设备写入尚未完成；提前公开会让其他request读到部分状态。这里只在显式成功完成后发布，失败则撤销，lease未释放的锚点不可驱逐。
questions.example: 教学例：pending的640状态必须查不到；失败后删除，不能用全零状态代替成功检查点。

questions.question: held-out视图是多给student一台摄像头吗？
questions.answer: 不是。它只由teacher产生目标；student和predictor必须根据其他context视图推断它，推理时也不要求该额外观察。
questions.example: 教学例：遮住背面照片，只给正面和侧面；背面latent只在loss端使用。

questions.question: 为什么Eq4不能先对每个view的loss求平均？
questions.answer: mask数量可能不同；论文给每个监督token同等权重，而不是每个view同等权重。还要先逐example归一化，再平均batch。
questions.example: 教学例：两个context各1和3个mask，加held-out4个token；总共8个目标等权，不是三组各占三分之一。

questions.question: MV-JEPA和Time-JEPA都用额外监督，目标能互换吗？
questions.answer: 不能。前者是跨摄像头latent并需要联合view predictor；后者是对齐物理时序并有unmasked回归分支。二者训练目标都不应变成student输入。
questions.example: 教学例：速度标量属于Time-JEPA物理head，背面视图的一组token属于MV-JEPA held-out query；换标签不等于同一任务。

questions.question: 怎样检查held-out和masked context没有偷进student？
questions.answer: 固定view ID，任意改held-out内容或被mask的context token，predictor输出应不变；这些改动可改变teacher目标/loss，但不能产生held-out输入梯度。teacher参数也必须无梯度，只做显式EMA。
questions.example: 教学例：把held-out token乘30后，预测不变而目标可变；若预测变化，就有训练输入泄漏。

fields.question: Why can resident KV pages still fail to reuse a hybrid prefix?
fields.answer: Recurrent state is overwritten in place. Resumption needs the exact matching checkpoint; a later state cannot simply be truncated to an earlier one.
fields.example: Illustration: KV reaches640tokens but the nearest state is at528; the native model must recompute the remainder.

fields.question: Do two restores by one request make a checkpoint proven?
fields.answer: No. Promotion needs at least two distinct restoring requests, or an already-known branch. Otherwise ordinary single-successor conversation anchors would all become protected.
fields.example: Illustration: repeated restores by b remain tier2; restores by both b and c qualify for tier3.

fields.question: Do FrontierReplay and ReplaySSM solve the same problem because both log inputs?
fields.answer: No. ReplaySSM targets decode-state writes, output-only computation and speculative rollback; FrontierReplay targets checkpoint production and retention at prefill structural boundaries. Similar algebra does not share serving policies, precision contracts or evidence.
fields.example: Illustration: a correct sixteen-step decode refresh does not prove that a next-turn template boundary was saved and remains reachable.

fields.question: Why must lookup exclude a checkpoint immediately after prepare?
fields.answer: Prepare only reserves a slot; device writes may be incomplete. Publication before completion could expose partial state. This component publishes only explicit success, removes failed reservations and never evicts leased anchors.
fields.example: Illustration: a pending640-token state must miss; failure removes it rather than publishing zero state.

fields.question: Is the held-out view an extra camera input to the student?
fields.answer: No. Only the teacher turns it into a target. The student and predictor infer it from other contexts, and inference does not require that additional observation.
fields.example: Illustration: provide front and side views, while a hidden back view supplies targets only at the loss.

fields.question: Why not average a loss for each view before applying Eq4?
fields.answer: Views may have different mask counts. The paper weights supervised tokens equally, not views, and normalizes each example before batch averaging.
fields.example: Illustration: contexts with one and three masked tokens plus four held-out tokens create eight equally weighted targets, not three equally weighted groups.

fields.question: Can MV-JEPA and Time-JEPA swap their additional targets?
fields.answer: No. MV-JEPA predicts cross-camera latents through a joint-view predictor; Time-JEPA aligns physical sequences through an unmasked regression branch. Neither target should become a student input.
fields.example: Illustration: a velocity scalar belongs to a physical head; back-view tokens belong to held-out queries. Replacing labels does not preserve the task.

fields.question: How do we test that held-out and masked context observations do not leak?
fields.answer: With fixed view IDs, changing held-out values or masked context tokens must leave predictor outputs unchanged. Teacher targets/loss may change, but held-out inputs must receive no gradient. Teacher parameters remain gradient-free and update only by explicit EMA.
fields.example: Illustration: multiplying held-out tokens by30 may change targets but not predictions; changing predictions reveals input leakage.
